title: Secure Sanity write path for saving posts
description: Design and implement how the component persists posts to Sanity. Per blog-implementation-guide.md (problems #1 and #8), writes need an elevated token and the free-plan 'Editor' role does not exist — a Viewer-scoped token returns `403 permission "create" required`. The write token MUST NOT ship in the client bundle. Define the contract: the component calls a host-provided save function / signing endpoint (or receives a write token injected at runtime by the host's backend), and that layer performs the create/update against Sanity. Document the trade-off (self-hosted signing endpoint vs Sanity Growth plan with a real Editor role).
acceptance_criteria: The component never embeds a Sanity write token in client-shippable code.
A documented save interface lets the host supply a write-capable function or endpoint; the component calls it to create/update a post.
Creating and updating a post round-trips correctly (write then read back) in a test using a mocked write layer.
The token/permission constraint and the signing-endpoint-vs-Growth-plan trade-off are documented for consumers.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body: RESOLVED by sanity-writes research (skill at .claude/skills/sanity-writes/). DECISION: the component is token-agnostic — it never imports/sees a write token. The host injects a `SanityWriteAdapter` with `save(post) => Promise<{_id}>` and `uploadImage(file, meta?) => Promise<SanityImageValue>`. Default backing adapter = a small server-side signing/proxy endpoint in the consuming project (useCdn:false, pinned apiVersion). KEY CORRECTION: an Administrator-scoped token works on ANY plan including FREE — Growth ($15/mo Editor role) is only needed for a real human Editor role, NOT a hard requirement. A Viewer token can never write (that's the 403). Build TASK-005 as the adapter contract + types; the actual signing endpoint is host-supplied (document it, optionally ship a reference impl).
